Criterion: Verify that, for rotary wing air vehicles, the effects of high-energy, low-frequency vibrations, generated by main rotor blade passage (fundamental and harmonic) frequencies at all engine and related component operating speeds and powers, do not adversely affect the operation of the engine and the drive system. Standard: Vibrations induced by the airframe rotor combination (including the tail rotor) do not exceed engine limits within the aircraft and engine operational envelope or adversely affect the operation of the drive system. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, and review of documentation. Verification is by engine test and ground/flight test. During ground/flight test, vibration levels of engine and drive train components are monitored throughout the operating range of the air vehicle at all applicable rotor speeds, aircraft gross weights, and center of gravity limits. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.4.1.8, A.4.4.1.8 for engine vibration and dynamic response 14 CFR 29.907

Standard: The rotary-wing drive system, including housings, gearing, shafting, couplings, and air vehicle mounting locations are designed to be free from damaging resonant frequencies at all operating speeds and powers throughout the flight envelope of the air vehicle including any effects of high-energy, low frequency vibrations generated by the main and tail rotor systems. Components should be free of damaging resonant frequencies at designed operating speeds and a minimum of ±20% of those operating speeds. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documents (e.g. system configuration descriptions, design data records, hardware drawings, inspection reports, and ICD requirements) to verify vibration characteristics requirements are defined in the drive system design specifications. Analysis.
  (1) Conduct resonant frequency and modal analysis of all transmission system components (e.g., housings, gearing, shafting, couplings, and air vehicle mounting locations) throughout the envelope of rated torque and speeds for the air vehicle to substantiate no damaging resonance modes exist.
  (2) Conduct analysis of air vehicle rotor system vibrations for impacts to transmission system components and substantiate no damaging vibration modes exist.
  (3) Conduct a stress response analysis based on the frequency responses of Analysis MoC (1) and Analysis MoC (2) to determine if the drive system has positive stress margins to address vibrational impacts. Test.
    (1) Lab test: Conduct component-level RAP testing of components to confirm modal predictions in analytical design.
    (2) Lab test: Conduct a gear resonance frequency test to verify vibratory modes. The dynamic stress levels in each gear are measured in locations sensitive to all significant vibratory modes. A speed scan from zero to the speed of maximum overspeed is performed with: a. Minimum load. b. Approximately 50% load. c. Maximum load.
    (3) Ground test: Conduct ground air vehicle testing to verify absence of resonant frequencies in the drive system.
